## This week

You posted 11 videos this week. That's up from 9 last week. But views slowed down. Last week your typical video landed around 6,016 views. This week that dropped to about 1,944 views. Your best video this week was the one that starts with "made this video talking about how I made 200k in 3 months," pulling 6,821 views. Your weakest was the one that starts with "i'm obsessed w paris," at 1,229 views. You've got 3 videos still too new to judge, so don't count those yet.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

This is the real question, and here's the honest answer: you don't have clean proof yet. Your videos tend to pair certain topics with certain filming styles every time, so it's hard to separate the two apart cleanly right now. You didn't post the same script twice this week in two different styles, so you don't have your strongest kind of proof yet. What you do have is this: what you talk about seems to matter more than how you film it. Where things stand right now: talk topic looks like the bigger lever, but you need to test the same script in two formats to know for sure.

## What is working

Your come-up videos, about how you got started, usually pull about two and a half times your normal views. You've posted 25 of these, so that's a real pattern. Videos with a link in bio call to action are your biggest winner, pulling almost 15 times your usual views, though only 8 of these exist so keep watching it. Your relatable everyday life videos are your weakest spot, sitting at about a third fewer views than normal, and you posted 7 of those this week, way more than usual.

## Try this next week

Take one of your come-up stories and film it two ways, once talking to camera and once as voice over footage, so you can finally see if the style matters or just the topic does. Add a link in bio call to action to your next couple videos since that's your strongest pull. Pull back on the everyday life Paris trip videos this week and swap in another come-up or real money numbers video instead.

best.md: Your video is running below what you normally pull in. Right now it has 2845 views after 2 days, while a normal video of yours sits at 4065 total. Your opening line was "monaco i frickin love you" shown as text on the clip, with no spoken hook. That style of hook usually does just fine for you, so the flat start here likely didn't stop the scroll or pull people into the next few seconds. Since the whole video is only 6 seconds and it's a single moment clip, there isn't much happening after the opening to keep people watching once they're in. There was also no call to action, so people had nothing to do when it ended. Next time, add a short line asking people to comment or share, placed right after the opening moment, not tacked on at the very end.

worst.md:
This video did badly. You got 473 views, but a normal video of yours gets 4,076. That is way under your usual.

Your opening line was "My biggest thing right now is everyone's like, oh, don't talk about money like it's not classy." It sets up a topic, but it does not stop the scroll fast. It reads like the middle of a thought, not a hook that grabs someone in the first 3 seconds. And it does not build a clear question that makes someone need to know what happens next.

After that, the video turns into a rant that jumps between money, travel, and being single. It has energy, but it does not keep giving people a fresh reason to stay. It feels like it wanders instead of building.

There was no call to action on this one. Since people were already interested in your money and lifestyle talk, you could have asked them to comment their own money mindset or share if they relate.

Next time, open with a sharp, specific line that makes people wait for the payoff, like a bold claim or a mini cliffhanger, instead of easing into the topic.
